text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice in software development where developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start, and the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. CI pipelines make this process smooth by automatically building, testing, and sometimes deploying the software. As a result, developers can find and fix bugs faster, and the final product is more reliable. CI saves time and reduces stress for the whole team.
